reply:
Let’s resume the comparison of two sentence prefixes ending in the same token:

• “She deposited cash at the bank”
• “She watched ducks by the bank”

Assume the same tokenizer makes the final “bank” exactly the same vocabulary token in both. Its token ID identifies the same vocabulary entry. In a simple two-stage picture, that entry supplies a starting vector, a list of numbers representing the token.

The context-processing model then uses the preceding tokens to calculate a contextual representation. “Deposited cash” and “watched ducks” provide different information, so the final representation can differ even though the token ID and its vocabulary lookup stay the same. We can treat the model’s internal machinery as a black box for now.

This is the bridge to contextual meaning: identifying the token and interpreting its use are two separate jobs.
